=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:2:28:16#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 2:28 | تَرْجِعُونَ ===
تَرْجِعُونَ (tarjiʿūna) — Pss, mutawatir: "Active voice reading (Form I active): ""you return"" — restores human agency to the act of returning, contrasting with standard passive turjaʿūna ""you are returned."" The shift from passive to active changes whether the return is imposed or voluntary."

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:2:29:3#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 2:29 | خَلَقَ ===
خَلَقَ (khalaqa) — —, mutawatir: Standard reading: Form I perfect active.

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:2:30:30#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 2:30 | إِنِّيَ ===
إِنِّيَ (inniya) — canonical, mutawatir: Fatḥa on yāʾ (inniya) vs. sukūn (innī) — canonical variant, no semantic change, phonological variation in pause vs. connection

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:2:106:2#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 2:106 | نُنْسِخْ ===
نُنْسِخْ (nunsikh) — Vr, mutawatir: "Canonical variant: Form IV (nunsikh = ""we cause to abrogate / we cause to copy"") vs. standard Form I (nansakh = ""we abrogate"") — Form IV introduces an intermediary: God causes someone else to perform the abrogation, or causes the sign itself to be superseded"

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:2:106:6#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 2:106 | نَنْسَأْهَا ===
نَنْسَأْهَا (nansaʾhā) — Vr, mutawatir: "Ibn Kathīr: root n-s-ʾ (to defer/delay) replaces n-s-y (to forget) — ""we delay it"" vs. ""we cause it to be forgotten""; introduces temporal postponement rather than cognitive erasure"

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:2:185:6#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 2:185 | الْقُرَانُ ===
الْقُرَانُ (al-qurānu) — hmz, mutawatir: Without hamza — softening of the glottal stop, a well-attested canonical reading (Ibn Kathīr)

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:2:185:39#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 2:185 | الْيُسُرَ ===
الْيُسُرَ (al-yusura) — skn, mutawatir: With ḍamma on sīn instead of sukūn — fuller phonetic form, no semantic change; an attested ten-reader variant

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:2:185:45#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 2:185 | الْعُسُرَ ===
الْعُسُرَ (al-ʿusura) — skn, mutawatir: With ḍamma on sīn — fuller phonetic form paralleling al-yusura; symmetric variant with the ease reading

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:2:185:48#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 2:185 | وَلِتُكَـمِّلُوا ===
وَلِتُكَـمِّلُوا (wa-li-tukammilū) — Vr, mutawatir: Form II (tukammilū) instead of Form IV (tukmilū) — intensive completion, emphasizing thoroughness and meticulousness of the completing act

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:2:219:7#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 2:219 | فِيهُمَا ===
فِيهُمَا (fīhumā) — vhr, mutawatir: Vowel shift: kasra to ḍamma on hā — fīhimā (standard) vs fīhumā; both grammatically valid dual pronouns

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:2:219:9#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 2:219 | كَثِيرٌ ===
كَثِيرٌ (kathīrun) — Dot, mutawatir: "Dot-variant: bā' → thā' shifts k-b-r (greatness) to k-th-r (abundance) — sin becomes ""prolific"" not ""great"""

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:2:219:24#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 2:219 | الْعَفْوُ ===
الْعَفْوُ (al-ʿafwu) — CE, mutawatir: Nominative variant: al-ʿafwu (ḍamma) = subject/predicate reading vs al-ʿafwa (fatḥa) = object reading — restructures syntax

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:2:258:6#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 2:258 | إِبْرَاهَامَ ===
إِبْرَاهَامَ (Ibrāhāma) — Lvw, mutawatir: Long-vowel variant — ā instead of ī in penultimate syllable. Reflects dialectal variation in the arabicization of the Hebrew name. Both are canonical readings.

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:2:258:15#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 2:258 | إِبْرَاهَامُ ===
إِبْرَاهَامُ (Ibrāhāmu) — Lvw, mutawatir: Long-vowel variant ā replacing ī — identical to word 6 variant, reflects consistent dialectal reading across the ayah

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:2:258:16#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 2:258 | رَبِّي ===
رَبِّي (rabbī) — Y-iḍ, mutawatir: Quiescent yāʾ vs. open yāʾ — rabbī (possessive with sukūn) vs. rabbiya (with fatḥa). The fatḥa form is more emphatic in declaration.

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:2:258:22#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 2:258 | أَنَآ ===
أَنَآ (anā) — madd, mutawatir: Extended vowel (madd) on final alif — lengthened pronunciation. Dialectal variation between short and long final vowel on the pronoun.

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:2:258:27#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 2:258 | إِبْرَاهَامُ ===
إِبْرَاهَامُ (Ibrāhāmu) — Lvw, mutawatir: Long-vowel variant — consistent with words 6 and 15. All three Ibrahim instances receive the same variant.

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:3:49:5#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 3:49 | إِسْرَا•ىيلَ ===
إِسْرَا•ىيلَ (Isrā˚īla) — hmz, mutawatir: Hamza variant — different treatment of the glottal stop in the name

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:3:49:13#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 3:49 | إِنِّيَ ===
إِنِّيَ (inniya) — in↔an, mutawatir: "Inna reading = independent assertion ""Indeed I..."" rather than subordination — shifts syntactic embedding to direct speech"

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:3:49:13#2 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 3:49 | أَنِّيَ ===
أَنِّيَ (anniya) — Y-iḍ, mutawatir: Variant vocalization of the pronoun suffix — no semantic change, dialectal variant

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:3:49:13#3 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 3:49 | أَنِّي ===
أَنِّي (annī) — , mutawatir: Base canonical reading with standard pronoun suffix

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:3:49:19#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 3:49 | كَهَيَّةِ ===
كَهَيَّةِ (ka-hayyati) — hmz|Assim, mutawatir: Assimilation of hamza: hayʾa → hayya — phonological variant, no semantic change

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:3:49:20#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 3:49 | الطَّائِرِ ===
الطَّائِرِ (al-ṭāʾiri) — Lvw, mutawatir: "Active participle form: ""the flying one"" — shifts from collective noun (species) to singular agent (one that flies)"

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:3:49:26#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 3:49 | طَيْرًا ===
طَيْرًا (ṭayran) — , mutawatir: Base canonical reading — indefinite singular/collective

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:3:49:26#2 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 3:49 | طَائِرًا ===
طَائِرًا (ṭāʾiran) — Lvw, mutawatir: "Active participle: ""a flying one"" — emphasizes the act of flying over the species-category ""bird"""

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:3:49:50#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 3:49 | بُيُوتِكُمْ ===
بُيُوتِكُمْ (buyūtikum) — , mutawatir: Base canonical reading with ḍamma on bāʾ

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:3:49:50#2 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 3:49 | بِيُوتِكُمْ ===
بِيُوتِكُمْ (biyūtikum) — vw, mutawatir: Kasra on bāʾ — dialectal vowel variant, no semantic change

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:4:42:9#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 4:42 | تَسَوِّىٰ ===
تَسَوِّىٰ (tasawwī) — Vr, mutawatir: Active voice Form II with tāʾ-marbūṭa of ta-faʿʿul origin or imperfect active — the earth itself performs the leveling (active agent), rather than being passively leveled

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:4:42:9#2 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 4:42 | تَسَّوَّىٰ ===
تَسَّوَّىٰ (tassawwā) — Assim|Gm, mutawatir: "Assimilation of tāʾ into sīn — Form V tataṣawwā with ta- assimilated; the earth ""makes itself level"" — reflexive reading: the earth voluntarily levels itself upon them"

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:4:42:11#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 4:42 | بِهِمِ ===
بِهِمِ (bihimi) — vhr, mutawatir: Kasra on mīm instead of ḍamma — different liaison vowel; some readers use kasra as the default pre-pausal or pre-consonantal form

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:4:42:11#2 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 4:42 | بِهُمُ ===
بِهُمُ (bihumu) — vhr, mutawatir: Ḍamma on hāʾ (bihumu vs bihimu) — dialectal variation in pronoun voweling; Ḥijāzī vs Tamīmī realization of 3mp pronoun

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:4:43:31#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 4:43 | جَا أَحَدٌ ===
جَا أَحَدٌ (jā aḥadun) — hmz|Cs, mutawatir: Hamza elision with compensatory lengthening — jāʾa becomes jā by dropping the hamza; canonical variant in the Seven readings

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:4:43:31#2 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 4:43 | جَاءَ •حَدٌ ===
جَاءَ •حَدٌ (jāʾa ˚aḥadun) — hmz, mutawatir: Hamza modification on aḥad — the initial hamza of aḥad is softened or elided while jāʾa retains its hamza; canonical variant affecting the junction between the two words

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:4:43:31#3 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 4:43 | جَاءَ‿احَدٌ ===
جَاءَ‿احَدٌ (jāʾā ḥadun) — hmz|madd, mutawatir: Hamza elision with compensatory madd (lengthening) — the two hamzas at the junction merge into a lengthened ā; canonical phonetic assimilation

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:4:43:31#4 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 4:43 | جِاءَ أَحَدٌ ===
جِاءَ أَحَدٌ (jēʾa aḥadun) — im, mutawatir: Imāla (vowel tilting) — the fatḥa on jīm tilts toward kasra, producing a sound between ja- and ji-; characteristic of certain canonical readers

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:4:43:37#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 4:43 | لَمَسْتُمُ ===
لَمَسْتُمُ (lamastumu) — Vr, mutawatir: Verb-form reduction: Form III lāmasa → Form I lamasa — removes the reciprocal morpheme; reading of Ḥamza and Kisāʾī. Legally significant: Form I = one-sided touching (Shāfiʿī: any skin contact breaks wuḍūʾ), Form III = mutual engagement (Ḥanafī: euphemism for intercourse)

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:4:49:15#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 4:49 | فَتِيلًا اُنْظُرْ ===
فَتِيلًا اُنْظُرْ (fatīlan-u ‿nẓur) — vhr, mutawatir: Canonical variant: initial hamza of unẓur read with ḍamma instead of standard kasra linking — affects liaison between this ayah's final word and the next ayah's opening imperative; no semantic change to fatīlan itself

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:4:56:7#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 4:56 | نُصْلِيهُمْ ===
نُصْلِيهُمْ (nuṣlīhum) — vhr, mutawatir: Pronoun vowel shift: -him to -hum; standard dialectal alternation in pronoun suffix after kasra — no semantic change, phonological variant

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:6:68:18#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 6:68 | يُنَسِّيَنَّكَ ===
يُنَسِّيَنَّكَ (yunassiyannaka) — Vr, mutawatir: Form II intensive (tafʿīl) instead of Form IV — yunassiyannaka implies repeated/intensive causing-to-forget vs one-time causation in Form IV

الْمَيْتِ (al-mayti) — Gm, mutawatir: Light form mayt vs. standard

الْمَيْتِ (al-mayti) — Gm, mutawatir: Light form mayt paralleling the variant at word 10 — consistent lightening across both occurrences

وَجَاعِلُ اللَّيْلِ (wa-jāʿilu l-layli) — V↔N, mutawatir: Canonical variant: active participle jāʿilu instead of perfect verb jaʿala — parallels fāliqu in Beat A, making both predicates participial; layl shifts to genitive (iḍāfa)

وَجَاعِلُ اللَّيْلِ (wa-jāʿilu l-layli) — CE, mutawatir: In the jāʿilu variant, layl shifts from accusative (object of jaʿala) to genitive (iḍāfa with jāʿilu) — restructuring the syntax entirely

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:6:99:40#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 6:99 | مُتَشَابِهٍ اُنْظُرُوا ===
مُتَشَابِهٍ اُنْظُرُوا (mutashābihin-u ‿nẓurū) — vhr, mutawatir: Hamza al-waṣl read with ḍamma instead of kasra at the junction — a canonical phonetic variation in recitation affecting liaison between the two words

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:6:99:43#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 6:99 | ثُمُرِهِ ===
ثُمُرِهِ (thumurihi) — vw, mutawatir: "Ḍamma-ḍamma instead of fatḥa-fatḥa — thumur is the plural of thamar, shifting from collective singular ""fruit"" to explicit plural ""fruits"""

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:6:122:4#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 6:122 | مَيِّتًا ===
مَيِّتًا (mayyitan) — Gm, mutawatir: Geminated form مَيِّت vs simplified مَيْت — classical grammarians debate whether مَيِّت = currently dying while مَيْت = already dead; both canonical

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:6:128:3#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 6:128 | نَحْشُرُهُمْ ===
نَحْشُرُهُمْ (naḥshuruhum) — Imp, mutawatir: "First person plural — divine ""We gather them"" vs. third person ""He gathers them""; shifts from narrative about God to God speaking directly"

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:7:25:9#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 7:25 | تَخْرُجُونَ ===
تَخْرُجُونَ (takhrujūna) — Pss, mutawatir: "Active voice variant — ""you (yourselves) come out"" vs passive ""you are brought out."" Shifts agency from divine extraction to autonomous emergence. Canonical in 7 reading traditions."

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:7:164:16#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 7:164 | مَعْذِرَةٌ ===
مَعْذِرَةٌ (maʿdhiratun) — CE, mutawatir: "Nominative reading (marfūʿ with tanwīn) — shifts from accusative ḥāl/mafʿūl to nominative predicate: ""it is an exculpation"" (i.e., hiya maʿdhiratun) or mubtadaʾ: ""an exculpation [is our motive]"""

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:7:165:18#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 7:165 | بِيسٍ ===
بِيسٍ (bīsin) — hmz, mutawatir: Hamza elision: baʾīs → bīs; simplifies articulation without semantic change

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:7:165:18#2 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 7:165 | بِئْسٍ ===
بِئْسٍ (biʾsin) — Lvw, mutawatir: Short vowel + sukūn: compressed form; may evoke biʾs (wretchedness) as abstract noun rather than adjective

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:7:165:18#3 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 7:165 | بَيْأَسٍ ===
بَيْأَسٍ (bayʾasin) — vw, mutawatir: Metathesis of hamza: faʿlas pattern; archaic morphological variant preserving root consonants

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:7:169:47#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 7:169 | يَعْقِلُونَ ===
يَعْقِلُونَ (yaʿqilūna) — Imp, mutawatir: "3mp ""they reason"" vs standard 2mp ""you reason"" — shifts from direct audience challenge to third-person comment about the narrated group"

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:7:170:3#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 7:170 | يُمْسِكُونَ ===
يُمْسِكُونَ (yumsikūna) — Vr, mutawatir: Form IV yumsikūna vs standard Form II yumassikūna — IV = simple retention, II = intensive/repeated grasping; semantic shift from passive holding to active, effortful clinging

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:7:201:6#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 7:201 | طَيْفٌ ===
طَيْفٌ (ṭayfun) — Lvw, mutawatir: Canonical variant: ṭayf (phantom/apparition) vs ṭāʾif (circling agent) — ṭayf emphasizes immateriality and spectral quality, while ṭāʾif retains the active participle sense of a circling agent

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:7:204:3#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 7:204 | قُرِيَ ===
قُرِيَ (quriya) — hmz, mutawatir: Hamza replacement: the hamza in quriʾa is softened to yāʾ — a phonological variant that does not change meaning but reflects dialectal pronunciation of hamza

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:7:204:4#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 7:204 | الْقُرَانَ ===
الْقُرَانَ (al-Qurānu) — hmz, mutawatir: Hamza omission: the hamza between rāʾ and alif is dropped, yielding Qurān without glottal stop — a canonical variant reflecting continuous pronunciation

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:8:42:4#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 8:42 | بِالْعِدْوَةِ ===
بِالْعِدْوَةِ (bi-l-ʿidwati) — vw, mutawatir: Kasra on ʿayn (ʿidwa instead of ʿudwa) — dialectal variant of the same word, both mean valley-bank; the ḍamma/kasra variation is a well-known phonological alternation with no semantic difference

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:8:42:9#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 8:42 | بِالْعِدْوَةِ ===
بِالْعِدْوَةِ (bi-l-ʿidwati) — vw, mutawatir: Same kasra variant as word 4 — applies identically to both occurrences of ʿudwa

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:8:42:39#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 8:42 | حَيِيَ ===
حَيِيَ (ḥayiya) — Gm|Assim, mutawatir: Unassimilated form — ḥayiya instead of ḥayya; the two yāʾs are kept separate rather than geminated. Both are canonical (7-reader) readings, reflecting a morphophonological alternation

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:11:105:2#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 11:105 | يَاتْ｡ يَاتِي ===
يَاتْ｡ يَاتِي (yāt/yātī) — hmz, mutawatir: Hamza removal — ʾatā loses hamza, becoming yātī; smooths phonetic texture but no semantic change

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:11:105:2#2 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 11:105 | يَاتْ｡ يَأْتِ ===
يَاتْ｡ يَأْتِ (yāt/yaʾti) — waqf, mutawatir: Waqf variant — pausal form with sukūn on tāʾ, standard in stopping; no semantic impact

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:11:105:2#3 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 11:105 | يَأْتِي ===
يَأْتِي (yaʾtī) — Yz, mutawatir: Full form with final yāʾ restored — removes the apocopation, normalizing to standard indicative imperfect

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:11:105:2#4 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 11:105 | يَأْتْ｡ يَأْتِي ===
يَأْتْ｡ يَأْتِي (yaʾt/yaʾtī) — Yz, mutawatir: Combined waqf/waṣl reading — yaʾt in pause, yaʾtī in continuation; both canonical

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:11:105:4#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 11:105 | لَا تَّكَلَّمُ ===
لَا تَّكَلَّمُ (lā ttakallamu) — Assim, mutawatir: Assimilation of tāʾ — lā takallamu becomes lā ttakallamu with idghām; no semantic change but phonetic heaviness adds gravity

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:11:116:9#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 11:116 | بِقْيَةٍ ===
بِقْيَةٍ (biqyatin) — H, mutawatir: "Ḥamza reading: short i-vowel on bāʾ, dropping the tashdīd on yāʾ — biqya as a lighter nominal form, possibly verbal noun pattern (fiʿla) rather than faʿīla, shifting from ""lasting quality"" toward ""act of remaining"""

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:13:9:6#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 13:9 | الْمُتَعَالِي ===
الْمُتَعَالِي (al-mutaʿālī) — Yz, mutawatir: Full yāʾ retained in pause and connection — canonical variant; makes the active participle morphologically complete with visible yāʾ; no semantic change but phonetically fuller

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:14:1:1#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 14:1 | ا ل ر ===
ا ل ر (alif lām rā) — waqf, mutawatir: Waqf reading: each letter separated with sukūn/pause markers — emphasizes individual pronunciation of each letter as distinct unit

=== SEGMENT QIRAAT-ER:14:1:16#1 | source QIRAAT-ER | verses 14:1 | سِرَاطِ ===
